findings.description: All three A-outputs (A1, A2, A3) invent active exponential backoff retry logic INSIDE the republish/publisher operation. The actual code implements no such retry loop at this level: on a failed `batch_update_view`, the code marks the tab stale, writes a best-effort banner, and returns `published: false`. Retries happen at the cycle/sync level (next iteration), not within republish. The exponential backoff that IS in the code (via `runtime::run_with_retry`) operates at the low-level Sheets API call layer, not at the republish operation layer where all A-outputs place it.

A1 assumes pull-based retry polling via `should_retry_now()` and caller-driven re-invocation; A2 assumes blocking thread with `std::thread::sleep` inside republish loop; A3 assumes async `tokio::time::sleep`. None of these mechanisms exist in the actual republish method, which is synchronous, does not sleep, and does not retry—it only marks stale and returns.

Spec text SHEET-PUB-003 states 'retry with an exponential backoff schedule' but does not specify the layer (API-call vs. operation). A-outputs resolve this as operation-level (inventing), but the code implements API-level backoff via `run_with_retry` wrapping all SheetsApi methods, with no operation-level retry.
